object: The philosophical and scientific doctrine that every event is necessitated by prior causes operating under fixed laws.  The assumption that the universe is a clockwork mechanism — fully knowable, fully predictable — which undergirded Western science, governance, and economics from Newton until its dismantling at the Fifth Solvay Conference in 1927.
